archetypes.name: path-matrix
archetypes.rationale: Verify every Step 3 exit status from SKILL.md has an explicit Step 3.6 skip-or-run disposition, leaving no status unaccounted for in the routing matrix.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the complete LOOP_STATUS enum from SKILL.md and the Step 3.6 skip logic. For each status value (complete, converged, cap-hit, zero-findings-degraded-panel, revision-failed, tally-error, degraded-empty-collector, plan-size-trigger, plan-validator-defects, emit-plan-failed, panel-failed, main-agent-vote-required, cap-reached), determine whether the plan explicitly routes it to either run Step 3.6 or skip Step 3.6. Flag any status that reaches Step 3.6 by accident (no explicit skip guard) or that is silently dropped without a disposition. Also check whether the new skip breadcrumb lines proposed for panel-failed, cap-reached, tally-error, degraded-empty-collector, plan-size-trigger, and plan-validator-defects are placed before or after the Gate B short-circuit exits in SKILL.md, since a breadcrumb emitted after an early exit would never fire. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: cross-doc-sync
archetypes.rationale: Detect per-status routing contradictions between SKILL.md Step 3 logic and approval-gates.md Gate B and Gate C bypass tables.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the Gate B bypass list in approval-gates.md (tally-error, degraded-empty-collector, plan-size-trigger, plan-validator-defects, converged, cap-hit, revision-failed, emit-plan-failed, zero-findings-degraded-panel) against the actual SKILL.md Step 3.5 branching code. For each status, verify that the bypass or passthrough decision is identical in both files — paying special attention to whether converged and cap-hit enter passive-summary mode in SKILL.md but approval-gates.md describes them as bypassing Gate B entirely, and whether main-agent-vote-required appears in SKILL.md but is absent from approval-gates.md. Also check the Gate C table in approval-gates.md against SKILL.md Step 4b: confirm that every status listed as skipping Step 3.6 in SKILL.md also correctly appears (or is correctly absent) in the Gate C bypass enumeration. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: Confirm the proposed two-entry integration test is internally consistent with the real tally script path, artifact isolation model, and cursor advance semantics documented in SKILL.md.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the proposed two-entry integration test against three criteria. First, artifact isolation: the existing test suite uses a single global TMP for all cases; verify the proposed entries either reuse that convention or correctly introduce per-case isolation without leaving stale artifacts from entry 1 that would corrupt entry 2. Second, cursor advance semantics: SKILL.md advances the cursor only when plan-after-round-${ROUND_NUM}.txt already exists before the round launches; confirm the test fixture creates or omits that file in the correct order relative to the cursor write, and that the ROUND_CURSOR= value written by snapshot-plan-round.sh write-cursor matches the value the test assertions expect to read back. Third, tally script path: the stub exports point LARCH_TALLY_PLAN_ASSESSOR_SH at the real tally-plan-assessor.sh rather than a mock; verify the proposed test inputs (assessor output files, ASSESSMENT lines) are formatted exactly as tally-plan-assessor.sh expects, and that any EFFECTIVE_ASSESSORS=0 or ASSESSOR_VERDICT assertions match what the real script would emit for those inputs. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
